output.summary: A flowering tree or shrub native to China and Japan, Japanese camellia grows naturally in forests. Its leathery dark-green leaves accompany rose or white wild flowers, while thousands of ornamental cultivars offer many flower colours and forms. Its processed leaves can be made into aromatic tea and contain caffeine and catechins.
output.edibilityNote: Processed leaves are used to make aromatic tea and contain caffeine and catechins.
